glosses: The name of the first letter of the Greek alphabet (Α, α), followed by beta. In the Latin alphabet it is the predecessor to A.
Latin alpha: the Latin letter Ɑ (minuscule: ɑ).
The name of the symbols Α and α used in science and mathematics, often interchangeable with the symbols when used as a prefix.

examples.text: I will attempt to make an alpha particle ("α-particle") with the Large Hadron Collider.

glosses: The return of a given asset or portfolio adjusted for systematic risk.

examples.text: To investment professionals, “alpha” is the return over and above the market return. If in a given year the S. & P. 500 returns fifteen per cent and an equity-fund manager generates a return of twenty per cent, his alpha is five per cent.
Similarly, alphas are 2.33% larger than that of the equivalent monthly alphas using compounded returns while no changes can be found using arithmetic returns.

glosses: A person, especially a male, who is dominant, successful and attractive; (see alpha male).

examples.text: Being a beta male in a species with alphas doesn't mean you have to sit out the mating game.
